r1-observability-1.summary: Investigation of notification-service shows that notification delivery delays began with high latency when communicating with external vendors (sms-vendor and push-provider) around 14:02 UTC, leading to message queue lag starting at 14:18 UTC.

findings.statement: sms-vendor send took 5519ms starting at 2026-10-12T14:02:53+00:00
push send to push-provider took 7278ms starting at 2026-10-12T14:06:19+00:00
Consumer group notif-alerts lag of 279 messages was recorded at 2026-10-12T14:18:26+00:00
Metrics query tool failed with 503 Service Unavailable, leaving metrics data unavailable.

open_questions: What caused the external vendors (sms-vendor and push-provider) to experience high latency starting around 14:02 UTC?

r1-dependency-2.summary: Retrieved service dependencies and recent changes for notification-service, event-bus, sms-vendor, and push-provider. Mapped all configuration changes, feature flags, and deployments across the platform for the past 7 days preceding INC-09.

findings.statement: notification-service depends asynchronously on event-bus and synchronously on sms-vendor and push-provider.
payments-api sends events to event-bus which is consumed by notification-service.
notification-service had a scheduled API credential rotation configuration change on 2026-10-12T07:38:00+00:00.
event-bus had a request timeout configuration change raised on 2026-10-12T05:21:00+00:00.
portfolio-service and auth-service had routine deployments shortly before the incident onset at 14:00.

open_questions: What specific error status codes or latency distributions are experienced by notification-service when calling sms-vendor and push-provider?

r2-observability-1.summary: Telemetry retrieved for sms-vendor and push-provider shows that sms-vendor experienced a p99 latency spike starting at 14:05 UTC peaking at 1569 ms, while push-provider metrics remained entirely normal.

findings.statement: sms-vendor p99 latency spiked starting at 14:05:00+00:00, reaching a peak of 1569.0 ms.
sms-vendor error rate and request rates remained stable around baseline levels during the 12:00 to 14:40 UTC window.
push-provider metrics (RPS, error rate, and p99 latency) showed no anomalies and remained entirely stable around baseline throughout the window.

open_questions: Why did push-provider take over 7200ms in log-00781 if push-provider metrics showed no latency anomaly?

r2-observability-2.summary: Telemetry verification shows that notification-service metrics backend returns 503 errors, and event-bus consumer lag began rising sharply at 14:07 UTC. Notification-service logs confirm high lag in the notif-alerts consumer group and slow downstream requests to sms-vendor and push-provider.

findings.statement: The query_metrics backend for notification-service returned 503 Service Unavailable errors after 3 attempts.
Event-bus consumer lag metric anomaly started at 2026-10-12T14:07:00+00:00, rising from a baseline of ~123 messages to a peak of 1006.69 messages at 14:33:00+00:00.
Notification-service logged slow outbound calls to sms-vendor starting at 14:02:53+00:00 (5519ms) and push-provider at 14:06:19+00:00 (7278ms).
Notification-service recorded consumer group notif-alerts lag warnings starting at 14:18:26+00:00.

open_questions: What caused the metrics backend for notification-service to return 503 errors?
Were the slow responses from sms-vendor and push-provider caused by external vendor degradation or downstream client-side saturation?

r3-observability-1.summary: Verified sms-vendor metrics around the 14:00 UTC window: latency_p99_ms showed an upward anomaly starting at 14:05 UTC and peaking at 1569.0 ms, while rps and error_rate_pct remained normal with no anomaly.

findings.statement: sms-vendor latency_p99_ms experienced an upward anomaly starting at 14:05 UTC, peaking at 1569.0 ms at 14:05 UTC from a baseline of 597.02 ms.
sms-vendor rps showed no anomaly in the 12:00-14:40 window, staying near its baseline of 88.69 req/s.
sms-vendor error_rate_pct showed no anomaly in the 12:00-14:40 window, staying near its baseline of 0.33%.
notification-service recorded slow sms-vendor send calls starting at 14:02 UTC.

open_questions: What caused the temporary spike in sms-vendor latency at 14:05 UTC?

hypotheses.title: External SMS Vendor Latency Degradation
hypotheses.mechanism: The external third-party vendor (sms-vendor) experienced transient internal latency degradation, causing synchronous outbound API requests from notification-service to block. This thread/connection exhaustion backed up the local notification message queue (notif-alerts), resulting in delayed SMS and push notifications for users.

supporting.note: sms-vendor latency_p99_ms experienced an upward anomaly starting at 14:05 UTC, peaking at 1569.0 ms.
Consumer group notif-alerts lag recorded starting at 14:18:26+00:00 as a downstream consequence of blocked workers.

contradicting.note: push-provider metrics showed zero latency or error anomalies, yet notification-service logged a slow push call in log-00781 (7278ms), suggesting local resource contention or thread pool blocking inside notification-service.

assumptions: The independent p99 latency spike on sms-vendor reflects genuine vendor-side processing delays rather than purely client-side connection starvation.

hypotheses.title: Notification-Service Client-Side Connection Pool Exhaustion / Thread Starvation
hypotheses.mechanism: The scheduled API credential rotation configuration change (chg-9140) executed earlier in the day on notification-service introduced latent inefficiencies in connection reuse or token refreshing, leading to connection pool saturation and cascading timeouts when calling external APIs under peak queue consumption.

supporting.note: notification-service had a scheduled API credential rotation configuration change on 2026-10-12 at 07:38:00+00:00.
push-provider took 7278ms in notification-service logs despite metric:push-provider:latency_p99_ms showing completely normal vendor metrics, pointing to a client-side bottleneck.

contradicting.note: chg-9140 occurred 6.5 hours prior to the onset at 14:02:53 UTC.
sms-vendor metrics independently showed an upward latency anomaly starting at 14:05 UTC on the vendor side.

assumptions: Credential rotation degraded connection pool efficiency or introduced synchronization locks that only manifested under peak concurrency.

hypotheses.title: Event-Bus Upstream Congestion
hypotheses.mechanism: Message broker queuing delays caused events to be delivered out-of-order or with delayed timestamps to notification-service, creating consumer lag that manifested as delayed end-user notifications.

supporting.note: Consumer lag anomaly started rising sharply at 14:07:00+00:00, peaking at 1006.69 messages.

contradicting.note: The first slow vendor call occurred at 14:02:53+00:00, before the event-bus consumer lag metric anomaly started rising at 14:07:00+00:00.
Event-bus CPU, error rate, and p99 latency metrics showed zero anomalies.

assumptions: Undetected broker-side partition buffering delayed event delivery.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: Symptom onset is established at 14:02:53 UTC via log-00763. H1 remains our primary hypothesis because sms-vendor metrics independently confirm an upward latency anomaly at 14:05 UTC, aligning with the observed slow calls. H2 captures the client-side possibility due to push-provider having normal vendor metrics despite notification-service logging a slow push call. H3 is kept as a low-confidence alternative since consumer lag started after the initial vendor slow call.
